body:
This will toggle each time this is called on the frame it was pressed, that doesn't seem correct, for example:
```gdscript
print(Input.is_action_toggled("foo"))
print(Input.is_action_toggled("foo"))
print(Input.is_action_toggled("foo"))
```
Will print:
```
true
false
true
```
If `Input.is_action_just_pressed("foo")` is true

It works perfectly here. I'm pressing the corresponding action and as you can see in the log below, it's doing the toggle

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66843277-9a16-4eba-90d5-6680ca7e9bae
the effect is TOGGLE.

Yes, but you're not paying attention, make your script:
```gdscript
print(Input.is_action_toggled("my_toggle"))
print(Input.is_action_toggled("my_toggle"))
print()
```
And you'll see

It *should* print:
```
true
true
```
or
```
false
false
```

But it will, when pressed, print:
```
true
false
```
or
```
false
true
```

Sorry if I didn't understand, but isn't the purpose of a toggle button to call it once every frame? I don't understand why you're using it like this in a loop. Forgive me if I'm being a layman and I don't even want to question you, because you know more about the engine than I do.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc4769c3-c896-4594-a26c-56e0e0952f64

It would be extremely confusing if `is_action_toggled` to *change* the state by calling it, rather than *checking* the state, this would be confusing IMO

Or perhaps more importantly:
Why would you want a method that does that? If we assume this isn't a mistake

I don't think this method makes sense to have only work as most would expect it to if you call it exactly once per frame
Why did you comment out the second line when testing this? That makes no sense when the second call is *exactly* what you need to test?

Sorry, but the Input.is_action_pressed methods, etc. are called on each frame. The toggle is also on each frame, in a loop. in logic like toggling value like for example: the player presses a button for the characterbody to lower. then presses it to raise it. for these logics and many others. I program games and I miss this in the engine.

No there's no requirement that they be called once on each frame:
```gdscript
print(Input.is_action_just_pressed("my_action"))
print(Input.is_action_just_pressed("my_action"))
```
Always prints either `true true` or `false false`, never `true false` or `false true`

But please do actually test the example I provided and see if it does output weird results

I think you didn't understand what a toggle button is for.

It's commented out because in a game you won't use the toggle twice in the loop. It doesn't make sense.

I'll check out your changes in a bit and confirm my theory, the snippet to use would be:
```gdscript
if Input.is_action_just_pressed("my_action"):
    print(Input.is_action_toggled("my_toggle"))
    print(Input.is_action_toggled("my_toggle"))
```
This is the expected behavior! It always prints true or false when pressing the button. You still don't understand what a toggle is.

In Unreal Engine, there is this toggle method. It maintains the state until it is pressed. When pressed, the state changes, that is, from true it goes to false and from false to true. You cannot use it as you are using it in the code twice, it doesn't make sense.

> You still don't understand what a toggle is.

I understand what a toggle is, and this isn't how I would ever expect it to work

> It's commented out because in a game you won't use the toggle twice in the loop. It doesn't make sense.

So the correct behavior should be that calling it should only toggle it once per frame, since you just want to toggle once per frame, right?

It's not productive if you ignore the feedback given, please go back to my comments and see what I mean and why this behavior is very confusing and unintuitive, any user would expect a method that *fetches* the state to not modify it

Further it's pretty unintuitive that the state is only toggled if you fetch it, meaning any input when you don't won't update the state, that would also be very confusing

But please open an issue and explain the need for this, and make sure to explain that the design includes that each call to this method toggles the state
I'm using the translator so I can explain to you and read what you write. Sorry if I came across as rude or anything, as I'm using a translator.
The language barrier explains you ignoring what I was saying, that makes sense 😄

It's not updating by frame! You didn't understand what a toggle button does. You can ask someone else for advice. Sorry, it's hard to explain through a translator. I only change the state when I PRESS THE KEY CORRESPONDING TO THE ACTION.

> You didn't understand what a toggle button does lol. You can ask someone else for advice.

Now this *is* rude and unhelpful

I have explained why this is confusing, please read again, and open a proposal

> I only change the state when I PRESS THE KEY CORRESPONDING TO THE ACTION.

This is not what your code does, it toggles the action only when the method is called and the action was just pressed, not if the action was pressed if you don't check

---

But this conversation isn't productive, please open the proposal and we can see what others think about this feature

The method name `is_action_toggled()` suggests that its only purpose is asking the question "is this action toggled?", which should mean that it is not supposed to do anything but give an answer "yes I am toggled" or "no I am not". The fact that the method itself is the thing doing the toggling is where the confusion comes from. I hope this helps clear things up.
